quiz.title: Less Inadequate, More Empowered
quiz.subtitle: Review the main teachings of the sermon about standing firm in God's strength, living in truth, trusting Him, and using the armor He provides.

quiz.startPurpose: Review the main teachings of the sermon and keep its message in mind throughout the week.

questions.question: Why does Paul tell believers to put on the armor of God?
options: So they can avoid every difficult situation.
So they can stand against the enemy through God's strength.
So they can prove that they are stronger than other people.
So they can depend on their own spiritual abilities.
questions.hint: Think about Paul's repeated emphasis on standing firm and relying on God's strength.
questions.explanation: The armor is not about becoming strong through ourselves. Paul calls believers to be strong in the Lord and to stand firm against the enemy by relying on what God provides.

questions.question: What question can we ask the Holy Spirit as we consider the armor of God?
options: Where am I already strong enough that I do not need help?
Which part of the armor can I ignore?
Where am I vulnerable?
How can I avoid facing spiritual battles?
questions.hint: The sermon encouraged us to recognize the places where we are most vulnerable.
questions.explanation: Recognizing vulnerability helps us stop pretending that we can handle everything on our own. The invitation is to let the Holy Spirit reveal where we need God's truth, righteousness, faith, salvation, His Word, and prayer.

questions.question: Why is the belt of truth important in spiritual battle?
options: Because knowing more information always solves spiritual problems.
Because Christians should never ask difficult questions.
Because truth is mainly useful for correcting other people.
Because the enemy's strategy includes deception and lies.
questions.hint: Think about the enemy's use of deception and the importance of knowing what is true.
questions.explanation: The sermon connected the belt of truth with the reality that the enemy uses deception. Standing firm requires us to recognize lies and hold on to the truth God has revealed.

questions.question: What does the breastplate of righteousness teach us about our identity?
options: Our identity depends on how well we perform each day.
We are made righteous in Christ rather than earning our identity through our performance.
We become righteous by comparing ourselves with other believers.
We must become perfect before we can approach God.
questions.hint: Remember the sermon's teaching about righteousness, identity, and our position in Christ.
questions.explanation: The sermon pointed to righteousness as something rooted in Christ, not an identity we manufacture through perfect performance. This changes how we approach God and how we live from the identity He gives us.

questions.question: What two traps did the sermon identify around righteousness?
options: Fear and doubt.
Pride and shame.
Legalism and lawlessness.
Comfort and suffering.
questions.hint: One trap tries to earn God's approval; the other rejects God's ways altogether.
questions.explanation: The sermon described two opposite ways of missing God's design: legalism, which tries to earn righteousness through performance, and lawlessness, which rejects God's standards. The gospel points us to righteousness received through Christ and lived out in response to Him.

questions.question: If someone feels they must clean themselves up before coming to God, what response fits the sermon?
options: Wait until they have solved their problems first.
Only approach God after they have had a good spiritual day.
Come to God in their present condition and trust the access He gives through Christ.
Avoid prayer until they feel worthy.
questions.hint: Think about what the sermon said about access to the Father even on our bad days.
questions.explanation: The sermon emphasized that we do not have to become perfect before approaching God. Through Christ, we have access to the Father and can come to Him as we are, trusting His grace rather than our own performance.

questions.question: According to the sermon, how should we respond to both pleasures and pains?
options: Trust God in both.
Trust God only when life is painful.
Use pleasure to forget about spiritual battles.
Avoid anything that could cause pain.
questions.hint: The shield of faith is about trusting God regardless of what circumstances feel like.
questions.explanation: Faith is not only needed when life hurts. The sermon challenged us to trust God in both pleasure and pain rather than allowing either one to become the foundation of our security.

questions.question: What danger can pain create when it pushes us away from God?
options: It automatically proves that God has abandoned us.
It can give the enemy a foothold.
It means we should stop praying until the pain is gone.
It guarantees that our faith will become stronger.
questions.hint: Remember the warning about unresolved anger and the opportunity it can give the enemy.
questions.explanation: The sermon connected pain, anger, and spiritual vulnerability. When pain is allowed to turn us away from God and remain unresolved, it can give the enemy a foothold rather than leading us toward healing and trust.

questions.question: How do the helmet of salvation, Scripture, and prayer work together in the sermon?
options: They help develop confident assurance in God.
They guarantee that believers will never experience doubt or difficulty.
They replace the need to trust God personally.
They are mainly tools for teaching other people.
questions.hint: Think about the sermon’s definition of biblical hope as confident assurance, not 'maybe it will happen.'
questions.explanation: The sermon connected salvation, God's Word, and prayer with biblical hope: a confident assurance in God. Scripture and prayer stir that hope and help us remain equipped and grounded in Him.

questions.question: Which statement best summarizes the central message of the sermon?
options: Spiritual battles can be avoided if we become strong enough.
The armor of God is mainly a list of rules for becoming better Christians.
The armor helps us trust God, live out the gospel, and stand firm in His strength.
Prayer is only necessary when we are facing a major crisis.
questions.hint: Bring together the sermon's teaching about God's strength, truth, righteousness, faith, salvation, Scripture, and prayer.
questions.explanation: The central message is not self-reliance. God provides what we need to stand firm: His truth, righteousness, gospel, faith, salvation, Word, and prayer. We are called to trust Him and live from what He provides.
